article.name: FERNme

contact.note: Checked the official pinned README and official project website; neither publishes a contact email. No email was inferred from account or commit metadata or third-party directories.

article.summary: FERNme is a user-personalization memory library with a deterministic weighted graph and event log, SQLite or Postgres stores, REST and MCP interfaces, and optional semantic search and proposal enrichment. The review records source observations only; no local benchmark or runtime result was produced.

who_what.text: The official README describes FERNme as the Fuzzy-Edged Recall Network, a user-personalization memory layer with a Python service, MCP and REST interfaces, and a graph UI. Its copyright notice names Acquilab Inc.; no maintainer identity is inferred from account or commit metadata. The project catalog supplies the explicit repository locator and Atlas attribution; the Atlas page is used only for roster context.

architecture.text: The core model separates a sparse per-user preference graph, a site-level association graph, and event records called the Cabinet. User edges store weight, confidence, source state, reinforcement timing/count, fast weight, salience, and stated/inferred provenance; optional typed entities and relations extend the model.

SQLite is the zero-setup store and Postgres implements the same store interface. Tables include per-(site,user) graph edges, histories, events, settings and consent, alongside optional entity, document, asset and audit tables; site-level association edges and population-prior state are separate.

Event mapping turns event type, item catalog tags and supplied tags into attributes deterministically. Hebbian updates adjust user and co-occurrence weights; retrieval compiles a bounded card by spreading activation rather than full transcript injection.

The official README lists REST, MCP, and a local graph UI, with optional document/photo integrations and opt-in local semantic search. These are documented interfaces, not end-to-end deployments checked in this review.

behavior.text: Write: observe requires consent, sanitizes tags/glosses, maps payload fields to graph attributes, updates graph state, saves it, appends a Cabinet event, and writes an audit entry. The deterministic hot path has no LLM call; separate proposal enrichment does not alter memory truth before acceptance.

Update/correction: repeated observations reinforce edges; edit creates a stated override edge that does not decay. Optional configured curation can demote conflicting older values and append supersede events; the source does not establish correction accuracy outside a measured probe.

Delete: delete and forget_everywhere remove profile data and recompute the site prior; forget_everywhere also records a content-free audit event. Optional managed files and photo data have corresponding purge paths. The inspected source cannot establish removal from backups, snapshots, or operator copies.

Retrieval: card applies activation over user state and an association view filtered by contributor threshold, ranks bounded attributes, and includes settings; recall queries Cabinet events by site/user and optional type/text. Optional local semantic search can blend embedding and keyword scores when installed.

Scope: core stores filter user-scoped data by both site and user and the service checks consent; remote bearer tokens bind to one profile. The project says REST/MCP identifiers alone are not a hosted multi-user auth layer, so embedding applications should supply authenticated identities server-side.

Provenance and evidence: graph edges retain stated/inferred provenance and source state; Cabinet events keep the payload and mapped attributes; audit entries are HMAC-linked and may use keyed memory references. These record application evidence but do not prove factual truth or source authenticity.

metrics.evidence: Spreading activation and bounded card selection are visible in source; no answerable probe or calibrated abstention workload was run.
Reinforcement, decay, overrides and optional conflict curation exist in source; post-correction recall was not evaluated.
Profile data, events, optional managed files, and prior contributions have delete paths; backup and replica propagation were not checked.
Per-site/user filters, consent checks and token profile binding are source-visible; no adversarial cross-scope probe was performed.
Provenance, Cabinet evidence, explanations and audit records exist; factual support precision was not measured.
No latency distribution or scheduled write-to-recall measurement was produced for this system review.
The source bounds the card and provides a token estimate, but this review ran no measured token/cost workload.
Sparse graph and prior structures are source-visible; persistent bytes per accepted item were not measured.
Audit verification and graph/history/health interface are documented; live telemetry was not collected.

limits.text: Source inspection cannot establish runtime quality, real-user usefulness, authorization supplied by an integrating host, or deletion propagation across backups and filesystem snapshots.

The official README labels its published benchmark inputs synthetic or LLM-authored, says FERNme does not win every recall benchmark, and describes a real-human pilot as pending. No such claims are treated as this review's independent measurement.
FERNme's security guide says its database is not encrypted at rest by the project and rate limiting is not implemented; production deployments need host controls.
No system runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run; this review is pinned to source SHA e1763d50cd3700bdb3db46f0903b8c28662edc8b.

benchmark.note: No FERNme runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run for this source review. Project definitions and fixtures are not FERNme measured results.
